guess: Primary: `/config set <key> <value>` accepts an UNKNOWN key and reports success - `parse_config_set_args`/`handle_config_set` validate the shape (two args present) but not the key against an enumeration of keys anything actually reads, so `/config set modle claude-opus-4-6` is silently accepted and the confirmation asserts the container (the write succeeded) rather than the payload (this key is real and will be honoured). Secondary: `handle_config_get` and `handle_config_set` disagree on their key universe or their source - one reads/writes the on-disk TOML while the other reflects live runtime state, so set-then-get can disagree, or set reports success without taking effect this session. Tertiary: any message in this file that lists valid config keys (a `/config set` usage line, `mcp_help_text`, or the `format_config_output` label set) is hand-typed rather than derived from the authoritative constant, and has drifted.
evidence: class precedent only, not a live sighting; planner had not read the file. Day 144 absorption class, Day 149 payload-vs-container, Day 142 mirrored structures, Day 140 hand-typed enumerations. No claim that any specific defect currently exists in HEAD.

what_i_found: Primary guess: MISS. `/config set` does validate the key — `handle_config_set` (src/commands_config.rs:672) routes every key through `crate::config::validate_config_value` (src/config.rs), whose catch-all arm returns "unknown config key '<k>' — settable keys: ..." derived from SETTABLE_KEYS, so `/config set modle claude-opus-4-6` is rejected, not silently accepted. Confirmed in HEAD. Secondary guess: PARTIAL HIT — right symptom (set reports success while get/load disagree, value never honoured), wrong mechanism. The split is not TOML-vs-runtime-state; it is TOML-vs-TOML precedence. `handle_config_get` (line 783) reads only `detect_loaded_config_path()`, the single highest-precedence file, while `/config set --global` writes to `~/.config/yoyo/config.toml`. With a `./.yoyo.toml` present, the write succeeds, the green "✓ Set k = v in <path>" line asserts the container (bytes landed) not the payload (this file is the one yoyo reads here), and the value is shadowed forever in that directory — a silent no-op dressed as success. Tertiary guess: MISS. The key enumerations in this file are not hand-typed: both usage lines (677, 792) call `settable_keys_list()`, which maps over SETTABLE_KEYS, and the unknown-key error derives its list the same way; `mcp_help_text` lists TOML sections, not settable keys, so it has nothing to drift from. Fix: added `existing_config_paths()` (all config files on disk, precedence-ordered), `shadowing_config_file()` (is the file just written outranked by one that exists?) and `shadowed_write_warning()`; `handle_config_set` now prints an honest ⚠ note naming the file that takes precedence instead of letting the ✓ stand alone. Additive, product-safe (no behavior change when no shadowing file exists), unit-tested.
